thread:
Aisha (docs): Heads up — I opened a tiny PR to reconcile wording across region docs. Noticed a few inconsistent uses of 'stored' vs 'processed' and some ambiguous region slugs. PR: https://git.redwood/example/region-terminology-audit

Sam K: :eyes: Looking. Which pages are affected? I can bump the SDK snippets while I'm here.

Aisha (docs): The Supported Regions landing and the Data Residency note on Private Deploy quickstart. Example sentence that caused Legal to flag: 'Data may be stored in multiple regions when overlap exists.' That could be read as us storing persisted customer data outside selected residency.

Priya (legal): Legal suggestion: be explicit. Draft language: 'Data processing (including transient routing and caching) may occur in multiple regions; persisted storage adheres to the customer's selected residency when the residency option is enabled (subject to applicable legal requests and compliance controls).' Also mention KMS/HSM: 'Encryption keys remain under customer control via KMS/HSM integrations for private residency.'

Maya R: +1. Also our SDK examples sometimes use shortened slugs like "eu" which is ambiguous. Can we standardize on the control-plane canonical slugs (e.g., eu-west-1)?

Jonah P: I'll update the code snippets. Proposed python example to put in the snippet block:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(region="eu-west-1", api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate("Translate this to FR")
print(resp.text)
```

And a curl example:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=eu-west-1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Sam K: That matches our control plane. Also propose a short mapping table snippet in the page: UI label -> canonical slug -> display name, e.g. "Europe (eu-west-1)". Minimal, one-row table.

Aisha (docs): On wording I'd like to replace 'stored' with 'persisted' and call out 'transient processing (caching, routing)'. Draft: 'Transient processing (caching, routing) may occur outside the selected residency; persisted data storage adheres to the chosen region when residency is enabled.'

Priya (legal): That is ok but add the compliance parenthetical we suggested. Also add a sentence about key control: 'Customers using private residency may integrate their KMS/HSM so encryption keys are customer-managed.'

Maya R: One more note: for on-prem installs we should add an explicit one-line note: 'On-prem packages perform processing within customer-managed networks; contact sales for air-gapped installs.' Cuts down on confusion.

docs-ci-bot: Running checks on branch docs/region-terminology-audit...
docs-ci-bot: Linkcheck: 1 broken link found -> https://old.redwood.ai/residency-whitepaper (404). Lint: passed. Spellcheck: passed.

Sam K: I have the replacement whitepaper link: https://redwood.ai/security/residency-whitepaper. I'll swap it.

Aisha (docs): Plan: I'll update the PR with legal-approved phrasing, swap the link, insert the canonical slug mapping table, add the SDK snippets from Jonah, and include the on-prem note. Keep the PR small and focused.

Jonah P: I'll follow up with a second PR if we need separate snippet variants for Dedicated vs Hosted (region flag behavior differs slightly). For this patch keep one canonical snippet that maps to control-plane behaviour.

Priya (legal): Ping me on the final diff and I'll sign off quickly.

Aisha (docs): @docs-ci-bot please re-run linkcheck after the link swap?

docs-ci-bot: Re-running linkcheck... OK, all links reachable.

Aisha (docs): Thanks everyone — merging after CI green. Target: small site patch today. :thumbsup:
